about.title: Cathedral City Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Cathedral City households rely on countless everyday products — kitchen appliances, power tools, vehicle parts, children's items — without a second thought. When a product fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or an inadequate warning, the consequences can be serious, and the path to accountability can feel confusing. California generally applies strict liability in these cases, meaning an injured person doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused harm. That standard can apply to manufacturers, distributors, and retailers alike. If you were hurt by a faulty product anywhere in Cathedral City or nearby areas of Riverside County, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney who can review what happened, explain your options, and help you understand what preserving the product and any packaging might mean for your claim.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Ease Your Burden
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent — only that the defect caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may broaden the options an attorney can explore on your behalf.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: An attorney can advise you on keeping the product, packaging, and receipts intact, since physical evidence often plays a central role in these claims.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often rely on strict liability, which generally focuses on whether the product was defective and whether that defect caused your injury, rather than on the manufacturer's carelessness.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product exactly as it was after the incident, including any packaging, instructions, or receipts. An independent attorney can advise you further once you're connected.
